original_record.question:
Werner folds a sheet of paper as shown in the diagram and makes two straight cuts with a pair of scissors. He then opens up the paper again. Which of the following shapes cannot be the result? <image1>
<image2>
original_record.solution: The shapes given in options $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}, \mathrm{C}$ and $\mathrm{E}$ can be obtained by cutting the paper as shown.  ![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2023_12_27_0f4ed2787981bb911326g-146.jpg?height=175&width=163&top_left_y=1350&top_left_x=524)  ![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2023_12_27_0f4ed2787981bb911326g-146.jpg?height=175&width=160&top_left_y=1350&top_left_x=888)  ![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2023_12_27_0f4ed2787981bb911326g-146.jpg?height=175&width=144&top_left_y=1350&top_left_x=1251)  ![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2023_12_27_0f4ed2787981bb911326g-146.jpg?height=175&width=158&top_left_y=1350&top_left_x=1600)  ![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2023_12_27_0f4ed2787981bb911326g-146.jpg?height=175&width=157&top_left_y=1556&top_left_x=1532)  The only one unobtainable in two cuts is $\mathrm{D}$, which requires four cuts as shown.

audit.explicit_conditions:
Werner folds a sheet of paper as shown in the diagram and makes two straight cuts with a pair of scissors. He then opens up the paper again. Which of the following shapes cannot be the result? <image1>
<image2>

answer_review.reasoning: Fold about the vertical midline. In the closed right half, A needs one straight segment at the top fold corner and one at the bottom fold corner; B needs two segments to remove a triangle at the fold edge; C needs one segment at each outer corner; E needs one top outer-corner cut and one bottom fold-corner cut. D has separate off-fold V notches at both top and bottom, each requiring two differently directed cuts: four cuts in all. Therefore only D is impossible with two straight cuts.
